quickAnswerTitle: Nebraska School Calendars Are Published Locally
quickAnswer: Nebraska does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. State law and Nebraska Department of Education accreditation rules establish minimum instructional hours, while each district publishes the opening dates, breaks, staff days, weather changes, and year-end dates families follow. In the current reviewed collection, Lincoln Public Schools begins selected transition grades August 12, 2026, and Omaha Public Schools begins selected grades August 19; their main calendars end May 20 and May 26, 2027, respectively.
about:
Nebraska school calendars are district schedules operating within a statewide instructional-hour framework. Nebraska Revised Statute § 79-211 sets minimum school-term hours, and the Nebraska Department of Education's Rule 10 materials distinguish 400 hours for kindergarten, 1,032 hours for grades one through eight, and 1,080 hours for grades nine through twelve. Those requirements do not establish one statewide first day, Spring Break, or last day.

The reviewed Lincoln and Omaha calendars show two different ways districts organize the same school year. Lincoln Public Schools uses a transition opening for kindergarten, grade 6 and grade 9 on August 12, followed by all K–12 students on August 13. Omaha Public Schools begins selected entry grades August 19, other K–12 students August 20 and Pre-K August 26. Lincoln's main student calendar ends May 20; Omaha's ends May 26.

Program scope matters as much as the headline dates. Lincoln publishes companion Middle School X/Y, Preschool and Full Day Preschool calendars. Omaha adds Early Childhood-only closures, grade-specific high-school testing attendance and a substantially different Wilson Focus Elementary calendar. Families should use the state rules to understand the minimums, the district calendar for systemwide attendance and school communications for building events, transportation, conference times and weather revisions.

calendarRules.label: Kindergarten has a separate minimum
calendarRules.description: Nebraska Department of Education Rule 10 materials list at least 400 instructional hours for kindergarten.

calendarRules.label: Grades 1–8 require at least 1,032 hours
calendarRules.description: The state framework is hours-based. District calendars may therefore differ in the number and length of student days while meeting the annual requirement.

calendarRules.label: Grades 9–12 require at least 1,080 hours
calendarRules.description: High schools have a higher annual instructional-hour minimum than elementary and middle grades.

calendarRules.label: Program calendars can differ inside one district
calendarRules.description: Districtwide dates may not cover every Early Childhood, alternative, focus, or specialty program. Families should use the official calendar for the student's program.

stateSections.label: Nebraska Uses Instructional Hours, Not One Statewide Date Count
stateSections.content: Nebraska's minimum school term is expressed in instructional hours. That allows local schedules to use different day lengths, late starts, conference closures, and program calendars while still operating under the same state framework.

faqs.q: Does Nebraska have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Nebraska establishes instructional-hour and accreditation requirements, but local districts publish their own opening dates, breaks, staff days, weather plans, program schedules, and last days. Families should use the calendar for their assigned district, school, grade, and program.

faqs.q: How many instructional hours does Nebraska require?
faqs.a: Nebraska Department of Education Rule 10 materials list at least 400 instructional hours for kindergarten, 1,032 hours for grades 1–8, and 1,080 hours for grades 9–12. District calendars determine how those hours are scheduled.

faqs.q: When do Nebraska schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no statewide start date. Lincoln Public Schools begins kindergarten, grade 6 and grade 9 on August 12, 2026, with all K–12 students in session August 13. Omaha Public Schools begins selected entry grades August 19, other K–12 students August 20 and Pre-K August 26; Wilson Focus Elementary starts August 4 under its separate calendar.

faqs.q: When is Spring Break in Nebraska in 2027?
faqs.a: Nebraska has no statewide Spring Break. Lincoln Public Schools lists March 8–12, 2027, and Omaha Public Schools lists March 15–19 for its main Spring Recess. Wilson Focus Elementary adds a Wilson-only closure March 22–26. Families should use their assigned district and program calendar.

faqs.q: Can schools in one Nebraska district use different calendars?
faqs.a: Yes. Lincoln publishes companion Middle School X/Y, Preschool and Full Day Preschool calendars. Omaha publishes a main District Calendar, an Early Childhood version with additional closures and a separate Wilson Focus Elementary schedule. These program calendars should not be treated as duplicates of the district baseline.

faqs.q: Can I add a Nebraska school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide ICS files that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. Each file is a one-time copy and will not automatically reflect later district revisions, school activities, transportation changes, or weather announcements.
